title: CE335: Plumbing Engineering
description: National Plumbing Code definitions, rules, and standards.

content.text: Plumbing is defined as the art and technique of installing pipes, fixtures, and other apparatuses in buildings for bringing in the water supply, liquids, substances, and removing wastewater and water-borne wastes.
Its primary purpose is to protect the health, sanitation, life, and property of building occupants by ensuring safe water distribution and effective waste removal.
A Plumbing Unit represents a standard minimum quantity of fixtures specified under Section 217.13, consisting of 13 total fixtures:

items: 1 Water Meter
1 Water Closet
1 Lavatory
1 Shower Head and Drain
1 Kitchen Sink
1 Laundry Tray
3 Floor Drains
4 Faucets / Hose Bibbs

content.text: Plumbing systems are composed of distinct categories of fixtures and devices:

items: Plumbing Fixture (Sec 217.10): Approved installed receptacles or devices supplied with water or receiving liquid-borne wastes. Note: Industrial or commercial tanks, vats, and process equipment are NOT classified as plumbing fixtures.
Plumbing Appliance (Sec 217.7): Devices performing special functions dependent on energized components such as motors, controls, or heating elements (e.g., water heaters, dishwashers).

Plumbing Appurtenance (Sec 217.8): Adjunct devices that serve a protective or regulatory function within the system without demanding additional water supply or adding discharge load (e.g., pressure regulators, backflow preventers).

content.text: Personnel levels, licensing, and organizational legal requirements are regulated under Republic Act 1378 (The Plumbing Law of the Philippines):

items: Apprentice Plumber: A beginner serving a required 3 to 5 year learning period as a helper to a journeyman.
Journeyman Plumber: A skilled individual fully competent to execute plumbing installations, maintenance, and repairs.
Master Plumber (Sec 214.5): A technically and legally qualified practitioner who holds a valid license under RA 1378, authorized to design, sign, and oversee plumbing installations.
Plumbing Firm (Sec 217.9): A legal entity or partnership where the majority of membership, stock, and executive authority is held by Registered Master Plumbers.
Plumbing Official (Sec 217.11): The administrative officer charged with enforcing the provisions of the National Plumbing Code.

content.text: Specific pressure parameters dictate system requirements to ensure functionality and prevent damage:

items: Inadequate Pressure: Supply pressure falling below 103 kPa (15 psi) is legally inadequate and requires installation of a hydropneumatic tank or elevated tank and booster pump system.
Excessive Pressure: Supply pressure exceeding 551 kPa (80 psi) requires the installation of an approved pressure regulator and strainer to protect piping and fixtures.
Water Hammer: A violent pressure wave/surge produced when moving fluid stops or changes direction abruptly.
Air Chamber: A capped vertical air space installed near valves that acts as a hydraulic shock absorber to cushion pressure surges.

content.text: Contamination prevention standards govern cross-connections and backflow risks:

items: Cross-Connection (Sec 204.24): Any physical connection or arrangement between a potable water system and an unpotable or polluted source.
Backflow (Sec 203.1): The flow of water or other liquids into the distribution pipes of a potable supply from unintended sources.
Back-Siphonage (Sec 203.5): The flowing back of contaminated water caused by negative or sub-atmospheric pressure in the supply line.
Airgap (Sec 202.6): An unobstructed vertical distance through the free atmosphere between the lowest opening of a supply pipe and the flood level rim of the receptacle.
Atmospheric Vacuum Breaker (AVB Sec 603.2.2): A backflow prevention device featuring a check valve and air inlet valve that opens to break a vacuum when fluid flow stops.

content.text: System integrity must be proven under specific test pressures held for a minimum of 15 minutes without leaking:

items: Water Test (Drainage/Vent): Filling the piping system in whole or in sections with water to inspect for leaks.
Air Test (Drainage/Vent): Subjecting system to a uniform gauge pressure of 34.5 kPa (5 psi) or 254 mm mercury column.
Water Supply Piping Test: Proving piping tight under a hydrostatic test pressure equal to the working pressure plus 50% (or an air pressure of 344.5 kPa / 50 psi).
